questions.explain: Bigger props — higher g/W — longer hover.

questions.q: A freestyle or long-range 5–7" with T/W 4–6: at what throttle should it hover according to the thrust table?
questions.explain: At T/W 4–6 the hover throttle is 30–41 % on the 0.65 thrust curve and up to 50 % on the square law (f-physics); 60–70 % means a T/W of about 2, with no margin for wind and maneuvering. The current in hover — no higher than ~40 % of the continuous rating.

questions.q: ESC continuous current relative to the maximum motor current:
options: Half as much, the ESC tolerates it briefly
questions.explain: A margin on current and voltage is the norm.

questions.q: What happens if you keep enlarging the battery for flight time?
options: The current drops because the battery is more powerful
questions.explain: A heavier battery → higher current; if it doesn't converge — change the aircraft class.

questions.q: Why does spare part availability matter?
questions.explain: The first repair will show it: an arm that is not on sale means the aircraft is grounded.

questions.q: What margin on current and thrust does the module recommend?
questions.explain: A 20 % margin pays for itself on the first windy day.

questions.q: Why are cheap components not always a saving?
options: They are not allowed on frames
They are heavier: mass is flight time and current
questions.explain: The price/mass trade-off: extra grams cost minutes of flight and amps.
